_comment: Thematic chapters for the N3-N1 points that belong to no near-synonym family. See scripts/build-curriculum.ts. A theme's job is to give the chapter a subject: the points inside it are related by function, not sequenced against each other. Anything not listed here falls back to alphabetical 'Further N* patterns' bucketing and is named at the end of a build:curriculum run.

themes.title: Windows of time and the moment something happens
themes.summary: While a condition still holds, the instant one thing turns into another, and how to say something is partway done or freshly finished.

themes.title: Trying, finishing, and leaving things as they are
themes.summary: Attempting something and failing, carrying an action through to the end, and the forms for an action left running or left undone.

themes.title: Without doing, and degrees of denial
themes.summary: Doing one thing without another, and the adverbs and set phrases that scale a negative from 'rarely' to 'not at all' to 'not necessarily'.

themes.title: Rules, habits and resolutions
themes.summary: Personal rules you set yourself, arrangements decided for you, and the ように forms for an effort made or an ability gained.

themes.title: Drawing a conclusion, and restating it
themes.summary: The わけ family for what follows logically from what you just heard, plus the という forms for defining, restating and introducing a topic.

themes.title: Emphasis and degree
themes.summary: Singling something out as precisely the one that matters, and the patterns that measure how far a quality or a situation goes.

themes.title: Cause and result
themes.summary: Naming what caused an outcome and what followed from it, including せいで for a cause you are blaming.

themes.title: Supposing, hoping, regretting
themes.summary: Setting up a hypothetical, wishing it had gone differently, and the forms for a hope expressed about someone else.

themes.title: About, according to, compared with
themes.summary: The に-marked phrases that fix what a statement is about, whose standpoint it is from, and what it is measured against.

themes.title: How things look, and how they stay
themes.summary: Pretending, resembling, and the られた form for a state that resulted from an action rather than the action itself.

themes.title: Everyday spoken shortcuts
themes.summary: The contractions, softeners and set phrases that mark conversational N3: checking a half-remembered fact, relaying a request, offering a gentle try.

themes.title: In other words, which means
themes.summary: The connectives that restate a statement more precisely, or draw out what it implies.

themes.title: Based on, centred on, in line with
themes.summary: The を- and に-marked phrases that name what something was built from, organised around, or made to follow.

themes.title: Worth the effort, or in vain
themes.summary: Whether the effort paid off: がい for something worth doing, かいがあって for effort rewarded, かいもなく for effort wasted.

themes.title: Halfway, gradually, prone to
themes.summary: An action caught in progress, a change still underway, and the suffixes for what something tends towards or is covered in.

themes.title: Can't, won't, and polite refusal
themes.summary: かねる for a refusal phrased as inability, and the patterns for what cannot be endured or cannot be afforded.

themes.title: Torn between two options
themes.summary: Weighing one course against another, and the forms for a wish that something could be made possible.

themes.title: Precisely because, and just because
themes.summary: からこそ for a reason you are insisting on, からといって for one you are rejecting, and the からsurrounding judgements in between.

themes.title: As you would expect of it
themes.summary: だけあって for something living up to its reputation, にかけては for where someone excels, and the patterns for a saving grace.

themes.title: Far from it, let alone that
themes.summary: どころか and its neighbours: correcting an assumption by overshooting it, and setting one thing aside to get to another.

themes.title: Along with, in step with
themes.summary: Two things moving together, one following the other, and the markers for what preceded or triggered an event.

themes.title: Reacting, feeling, finding it unbearable
themes.summary: ことに for the feeling a fact provokes, ものがある for an impression you cannot name, and the forms for excess and indifference.

themes.title: Not without, not unless
themes.summary: The double-negative conditions: what cannot happen until something else does, and what has to be got out of the way first.

themes.title: Whether one or the other
themes.summary: The paired literary patterns for listing alternatives, and for admitting you cannot tell which of them applies.

themes.title: Two things at once, two things alike
themes.summary: Doing one thing alongside another, roles held together, and the matched pairs that say two facts are of a piece.

themes.title: Only this, and nothing else
themes.summary: ならでは for what only one thing can offer, をおいて他に for the one remaining candidate, and the patterns that dismiss the alternatives.

themes.title: Scale, quantity and extent
themes.summary: からある for a figure you are stressing as large, というところだ for one you are playing down, and the suffixes for entirety.

themes.title: From whose standpoint, on what grounds
themes.summary: The literary からの/から言わせれば forms for whose view a statement is, and the phrases that name the basis it rests on.

themes.title: Granted that, but
themes.summary: こそ paired with a contrast: conceding one point emphatically in order to deny another.

themes.title: As if, seeming like, putting it on
themes.summary: The ごとく simile forms, the ぶる family for affecting a manner, and the suffixes for something that merely looks the part.

themes.title: It's not as if, it won't do
themes.summary: あるまいし for dismissing a premise, ではすまない for what cannot be left at that, and the forms for a duty that will not go away.

themes.title: Befitting the position, or not
themes.summary: たる for the standing something holds, ともあろう and にあるまじき for conduct that falls short of it.

themes.title: Turning points and starting points
themes.summary: The moment a situation changed: を境に for the pivot, を皮切りに for the first of a series, を経て for the process passed through.

themes.title: Forced into it, and the state it left
themes.summary: を余儀なくされる for a course forced on you, 始末だ for where it ended up, and the literary suffixes and exclamations for an extreme.

themes.title: Unfazed by it, aside from it
themes.summary: をものともせずに for pressing on regardless, をよそに for ignoring it, はさておき for setting it aside.

themes.title: No end to it
themes.summary: The きりがない patterns for something that cannot be exhausted, and ては/そばから for a cycle that keeps restarting.

themes.title: Without doing, without meaning to
themes.summary: The literary 'without' forms, ずじまい for a chance missed, and ともなく for something done without intending it.

themes.title: Not impossible, not unheard of
themes.summary: The hedged double negatives that concede a possibility without endorsing it, the literary potential form, and べからず for a flat prohibition.

themes.title: Worth it, or unbearable
themes.summary: に堪える and に堪えない for what does or does not repay the attention, 足る and 足りない for what measures up.

themes.title: When it comes to that
themes.summary: The となると/となれば family for a situation reaching a threshold, and the conditionals that follow from it.

themes.title: Depending on how it turns out
themes.summary: The のいかん set: one noun, three grammatical slots, all saying the outcome hangs on this.

themes.title: Naming a thing, and seeing it through
themes.summary: The という forms that name or generalise, ぬく for carrying something through to the end, and the phrases for what you did it in spite of.
